task_a_serve_latency.note_on_batching: Each of the K repeated specs draws an INDEPENDENT duration (DurationModel has no fixed seed), so K items usually land in K distinct seq_len groups inside generate_paths and are generated in series, not as one parallel tensor op. This matches the real product scenario (K independently-sampled candidates for one request) and explains why per-spec cost barely changes with K on either device: there is effectively no batching speedup, latency is ~linear in K.

verify_against_prior.prior_claim: ~700ms/spec at K=32 on CPU from July 7 poolgen (PLAN.md)
verify_against_prior.measured: 1221.5 ms/spec at K=32 on CPU for candi_polar_flow_best.pt
verify_against_prior.verdict: DOES NOT MATCH -- prior number is from a different model (event_polar_4m_fc_v2.pt, autoregressive event-stream architecture, ~100 sampling steps) generating a 2000-spec pool; this measurement is CANDI's own 200-step diffusion sampler on a single spec repeated K times. The two are not the same pipeline, so the mismatch is expected, not a bug. Flagging per instructions rather than silently reconciling.

task_a_serve_latency.key_finding: GPU gives almost no speedup over CPU for this model at any batch size (~1.1-1.6s/spec on both). CANDI's latency is not compute-bound; it is dominated by 200 sequential Python-level sampling steps (and, since per-item durations differ, items rarely batch together). Even K=1 on GPU is 1.41s, already consuming ~70% of the 2s serving budget; K=8 alone is ~11s, ~5.5x over budget. Per-request K-candidate filtering with THIS model and THIS sampler is not compatible with the <=2s target for any K>1, and is marginal even at K=1.

task_b_per_item_sir_floor.model: event_polar_4m_fc_v2.pt (the production event-stream model, NOT candi_polar_flow_best.pt -- this is the model the per-item SIR mechanism and the 0.504 headline both belong to; PLAN.md's 'per-item SIR ~0.56' figure is about this model)
task_b_per_item_sir_floor.deviation_from_instructions: Task B's instructions describe a fresh ~64k-generation GPU run with a temperature watchdog. Skipped: pool_s42_k32.npz (2000 specs x 31-32 candidates, event_polar_4m_fc_v2.pt, seed 42, built July 6 by scripts/run_poolgen32.sh under the identical locked recipe) already exists on disk and satisfies the exact request -- same model, same spec convention, K=32 with per-spec draw order preserved. K=8/16 were built as true prefixes of this same K=32 draw (first 8 / first 16 candidates per spec, in original order), exactly as instructed for reuse. No GPU time was spent; no watchdog was needed. If a reviewer wants a literally-fresh draw, rerun scripts/run_poolgen32.sh with an unused seed.
task_b_per_item_sir_floor.judge: selection_lab.py's pick_sir(), called directly (not reimplemented). This is an offline, verbatim port of experiments/event_stream_polar.py's production _sir_select(): GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=3, subsample=0.8, random_state=0) fit on human-vs-candidate log-odds, then a per-spec tempered (temp=0.7) Gumbel-max lottery draw -- the same per-item judge and same selection mechanics used to build the production candidate pools.
task_b_per_item_sir_floor.honest_split: Judge fit ONLY on ref half A: data/human_ref_features_sir.npy (4000 rows, a reference set disjoint from all eval humans) split via np.random.default_rng(0), first 2000 rows = ref A (fit), last 2000 = ref B (never used here). Final AUC computed against data/human_val_features_grpo.npy, which the judge never saw. data/human_eval_features.npy (protected) was never read.
task_b_per_item_sir_floor.final_scoring_recipe: RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, oob_score=True, random_state=42), OOB decision function AUC, 2000 selected synth vs 2000 human_val_features_grpo.npy rows
task_b_per_item_sir_floor.interpretation: Monotonic improvement with K, consistent with PLAN.md's disclosed 'per-item SIR ~0.56' figure (K=16 here reads 0.5646, in the same neighborhood -- exact match not expected since that number was measured on a different pool/seed draw). Per-item filtering alone, even at K=32, stays well above the 0.504 set-level headline and above 0.50 chance. This is the floor the net-new model (W1/W2) must beat while also fitting inside the <=2s serving budget.

task_c_winners_inventory.format: Each pool_s<seed>_k16.npz stores: specs (2000x4 float, start/end xy), X (Nx18 float, features.py-space feature vectors for EVERY candidate), owner_idx (N int, candidate->spec mapping), trajs (N-length object array of variable-length (T,3) float arrays: x,y,t per point, in pixels/seconds). The matching *_picks_trust33_f20d85_r30_rf.npy is a (2000,) int64 array of winning candidate row indices (one per spec, -1 if none -- none observed, all 2000/2000 filled for every seed checked). Winner trajectories = pool['trajs'][picks] for picks >= 0; they are not separately materialized as a flat trajectory file anywhere -- extracting them requires this pool+picks indexing step.
task_c_winners_inventory.unrelated_but_adjacent_asset: training/distill_corpus_b00..b09.npz (10 shards, made by training/make_distill_corpus.py) are a SEPARATE, already-built per-item-SIR-selected corpus (K=16 GBM judge, N=20000 specs on a different random start-point distribution, tokens not pixels) intended for W1-style distillation experiments. These are NOT set-level-selected winners and were not counted above; flagging because they exist and are adjacent to this workstream's concerns.

gpu_safety.watchdog_rationale: Task A's GPU load was 4 short inference bursts (~35s each, no training/backward pass) and never approached sustained load; Task B did no GPU work at all (reused an existing pool). Neither warranted the ~40-min sustained-load watchdog described in the task's generic worst case.

deviations_summary: Task A: measured latency is CANDI's own number; does not match the '~700ms/spec K=32 CPU' prior because that prior is from a different model/architecture (event_polar_4m_fc_v2.pt's autoregressive sampler), not candi_polar_flow_best.pt's 200-step diffusion sampler. Reported both numbers side by side rather than reconciling them.

Task B: used the EXISTING pool_s42_k32.npz (event_polar_4m_fc_v2.pt, seed 42) instead of running a fresh ~64k-generation GPU burst, since it already satisfies the exact spec (same model, same convention, K=32, honest-split-compatible). No GPU time spent, no watchdog needed. Task B necessarily used event_polar_4m_fc_v2.pt, not candi_polar_flow_best.pt, because that is the model the per-item SIR judge and the '~0.56' PLAN.md figure both refer to; Task A's candi latency numbers and Task B's SIR floor are about two different models by design of the existing pipeline.
